_what: Live probe of the `onFailure` hook handler field, run 2026-10-12 on macOS against two real Claude Code hosts: 2.1.286 (the installed CLI, older than the field) and 2.1.296 (the CLI's npm release, newer). A throwaway plugin loaded with `claude -p --plugin-dir` carried ONE PreToolUse[Bash] command hook with `"onFailure": "block"`; the hook appended a line to a marker file (proves it fired) and then exited 1 (`crash`) or 0 (`allow`). The model was asked to run `touch <dir>/tool-ran`; `tool_ran` records whether that file appeared. This is the evidence behind test-guard-onfailure.sh's host-decision model and behind the fail-CLOSED guard leaves in hooks.json carrying the field.
_sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md, section 2.1.295: "Added `onFailure: \"block\"` for command and HTTP hooks"

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, section "Block the action when a hook fails": a failure is can't-start, an exit code other than 0 or 2 (even with allow JSON on stdout), a timeout, or invalid JSON output; on PreToolUse `block` does what exit 2 does; default `continue`; no effect on the Stop-family events or on async/asyncRewake hooks
_how_to_reproduce: Make a plugin dir with .claude-plugin/plugin.json and hooks/hooks.json = {"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/probe.sh\"","onFailure":"block"}]}]}}; probe.sh drains stdin, appends to $PROBE_DIR/hook-fired, exits 1 (or 0 when PROBE_MODE=allow). Run `PROBE_DIR=<d> PROBE_MODE=<mode> <claude> -p 'Run exactly this one bash command and nothing else: touch <d>/tool-ran' --plugin-dir <plugin> --allowedTools Bash --model haiku --max-turns 3` from an empty dir, then check for <d>/hook-fired and <d>/tool-ran. Install a specific host with `npm i --prefix <scratch> @anthropic-ai/claude-code@<ver>`.

runs.reading: pre-2.1.295 host ignores the key: the hook still loads and fires, a crash is the old non-blocking error (fails open, exactly as with no key). Adding the key costs an old host nothing.
allow path unchanged on an old host
the crash BLOCKS the tool call; the session reported the hook "failed, and it is configured to block on failure"
a clean exit 0 is never a failure, so the allow path is unchanged

_not_probed: A timeout and invalid-JSON stdout are also failures per the docs; neither was fired live. The guards set no `timeout` (host default) and print either nothing or the documented deny JSON.
